subject: general
question: For a current carrying circular coil as we move towards the center from the circumference, the magnetic field strength

options.text: May increase or decrease depending on direction of current in the loop.

solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Biot Savart Law states that: The magnetic intensity (dB) at a point A due to current I flowing through a small element dl is Directly proportional to the current (I).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98c7b85f8ce250bf37f202d060dfebdb4ff35a7c1e6c0f27611ec65e11c8e008.png] 
 
• The magnetic field at the center of the circular coil is given by

 B = frac{{{mu _o}}}{{2 }}(I)/(r)

 Where B = strength of the magnetic field, I = current, r = radius or distance

**EXPLANATION__:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/721cb121c9e56fb795fd6f8d944f04ed6a04492bacdef197518fc6f60fc5b00e.png] 

 
• From above it is clear that the magnetic field due to the circular coil is **inversely proportional to the distance.**
 
• As we **move towards the center of the coil**, the **magnetic field strength increases**. Therefore option 1 is correct.
 
• This is **because the two magnetic fields from either end assist each other**.
 
• **The magnetic field** is **maximum at the center of the coil**.
